request.system: You are a precise classification engine. You reply with a code and nothing else: no explanation, no punctuation, no preamble.

messages.content:
Assign the three-character ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode of care described below. A three-character category is one capital letter followed by exactly two digits, for example J44.

Hospital course:
Patient Information: 
Name: Not specified
Age: 62
Gender: Male

Hospital Course: 
The patient was admitted to the hospital with complaints of abdominal pain and distension for the past month, which worsened in the last five days. The patient was diagnosed with small intestinal obstruction and underwent emergency laparotomy. During the operation, a small amount of food fiber was expelled, and multiple “stenosis rings” were found in the intestinal lumen at approximately 40 cm from the distal obstruction. The diseased bowel was removed, and the patient recovered without any discomfort. Pathological findings reported intestinal stenosis, mucosal erosion, and inflammatory granulation tissue formation. It showed neutrophil infiltration and vasodilation and congestion in the serosa. The muscle layer and serosa layer did not show any structural abnormality.

Summary of Hospital Stay: 
The patient was admitted to the hospital with abdominal pain and distension for the past month and was diagnosed with small intestinal obstruction. The patient underwent emergency laparotomy, and a diseased bowel was removed. The pathological findings reported intestinal stenosis and mucosal erosion. The patient recovered well without any discomfort. 
Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Condition at Discharge: 
Recovered.

Follow-up Plan: 
Patient was followed up for two months, and no discomfort was found. No further treatment is required at this time.

Reply with the three characters only.

text:
The picture is small bowel obstruction from multiple stenotic rings, with mucosal erosion and inflammatory granulation tissue. This pattern is typical of NSAID-induced diaphragm disease of the small intestine. The diagnosis section is withheld, so the category depends on how the obstruction is coded.

Candidate categories:
- K56 covers paralytic ileus and intestinal obstruction without hernia, and includes obstruction from stricture.
- K63 covers other diseases of the intestine, including K63.1 perforation and K63.8 other specified diseases.
- K31 covers stenosis of the intestine, but not in this context.
- K50 covers Crohn's disease of the small intestine, but the pathology does not support it.

Under ICD-10-AM, intestinal stricture and stenosis is coded to K56.6 (other and unspecified intestinal obstruction). The principal diagnosis here is the obstruction caused by the strictures, so K56 fits best.

K56
